descriptionChirho: Hananiah (Hebrew חֲנַנְיָה / חֲנַנְיָהוּ, meaning 'YHWH has been gracious'), a theophoric personal name borne by multiple distinct individuals in the Hebrew Bible. These include: (1) a Benjamite military commander under King Uzziah (1 Chr 25:4, 23; 2 Chr 26:11); (2) the false prophet from Gibeon who opposed Jeremiah, breaking the yoke-bars and prophesying the return of the exiles within two years, only to die as Jeremiah foretold (Jer 28:1-17, the most prominent bearer); (3) a postexilic leader who helped repair the walls of Jerusalem under Nehemiah (Neh 3:8, 30; 7:2; 10:23; 12:12, 41); (4) the Hebrew name of Shadrach, one of Daniel's three companions in Babylon (Dan 1:7); (5) a son of Zerubbabel in the Davidic genealogy (1 Chr 3:19, 21). All morphological variants (bare name, with conjunctions, with prepositions, long -yahu form) refer to this shared personal name across these distinct referents. Multilingual glosses consistently transliterate: حَنَنْيَا (Arb), Hananja/Chananja (Deu), Hanania (Fra), हनन्याह (Hin), 하나냐/하난니야 (Kor), Hananias/Jananyah (Spa).
